Developer Docs

# **Authorization**

Copy Markdown

* * *

Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token` , authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.

For a quick start, see the [Setup Guide](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/getting-started) . For Ramp's own MCP server and CLI, see Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI .

...

## Supported grant types

Permanent link: Supported grant types

|Grant Type |Use Case |User Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
|**Client Credentials** |Internal integrations, server-to-server |None required |
|**Authorization Code** |Third-party apps, public integrations |Authorized user consent required |
|**Refresh Token** |Renew access after an Authorization Code grant |None after the initial authorization |

...

`cards:read_vault` is available only to approved integrators; see [Virtual Cards](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/virtual-cards) . Scopes marked partners only appear in the partner Developer Console, not in a business's own Developer API settings. Some endpoints also require a Ramp plan feature and return `403` without it, even with the right scope.

* * *

## Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI

Permanent link: Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI

[Ramp MCP](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/ramp-mcp) and [Ramp CLI](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/cli) sign in with OAuth, but you don't choose scopes. A connection can do what the connecting user's Ramp role allows, within the access level chosen at sign-in.

When you connect, the consent screen asks you to choose **Full access** (the default) or **Read-only** . With the CLI, you can also run `ramp auth login --read-only` . A read-only connection gets read scopes only:

* Ramp MCP doesn't list tools that make changes.
* Write requests fail with `403 Forbidden` and error code `DEVELOPER_7100` ( `These scopes are not allowed for this token: ...` ). Through Ramp MCP, the agent sees this as a tool error.

To make changes, reconnect and choose **Full access** , or run `ramp auth login` without `--read-only` .

Unlike other apps, Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI get a new refresh token each time they refresh, and its lifetime restarts. Connections still expire 30 days after they're created; reconnect to renew. Who can connect is controlled by a Ramp role permission; see [Manage connected AI tools ↗](support.ramp.com/managing-connected-ai-tools) .

Third-party apps are unchanged: they get exactly the scopes they were granted.

...

## Token management

Permanent link: Token management

* **Format** : Access tokens are bearer tokens prefixed with `ramp_business_tok_` , `ramp_user_tok_` , `ramp_business_jwt_` , or `ramp_user_jwt_` .
* **Lifetime** : Client Credentials access tokens last 10 days (864,000 seconds). Authorization Code and Refresh Token access tokens default to 1 hour (3,600 seconds), and some apps have a different configured lifetime. Use `expires_in` from the token response.
* **Scopes** : A token can't be used beyond its granted scopes. To change scopes, get a new token. Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI tokens are limited by the user's role and access level instead.
* **Environment** : Tokens work only in the environment that issued them. Sandbox and production need separate apps.

## Treat tokens as credentials

Never log tokens or include them in error messages, store them encrypted, and send them only over HTTPS.

## Authorization flows

Permanent link: Authorization flows

### Client credentials flow

Permanent link: Client credentials flow

Use this flow for server-to-server integrations with your own Ramp business. Send `client_id:client_secret` , base64-encoded, in an `Authorization: Basic ...` header. Some apps are configured to send `client_id` and `client_secret` in the form body instead.

Pass the scopes you need as a space-separated `scope` field. If you omit `scope` , the token has no scopes. The token has business-wide access limited by those scopes, and there's no end user. Actions that need a user are attributed to the app's creator by default.

Client Credentials doesn't return a refresh token. Request a new access token when the current one expires. Keep the client secret on your servers, never in client-side code.

...

```
app.ramp.com/v1/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=https://yourapp.com/callback&scope=transactions:read business:read&state=random_csrf_token
```

...

#### Step 3: Exchange the `code` for an access token

Permanent link: Step 3: Exchange the `code` for an access token

Codes expire after 5 minutes.

Exchange code for access token

Shell

Copy

```
curl --request POST '{environment-url}/developer/v1/token' \ --header "Authorization: Basic $( echo -n " $CLIENT_ID : $CLIENT_SECRET " | base64 ) " \ --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode "grant_type=authorization_code" \ --data-urlencode "code=AUTH_CODE_HERE" \ --data-urlencode "redirect_uri=yourapp.com/callback"
```

  
#### Step 4: Refresh the access token

Permanent link: Step 4: Refresh the access token

To get refresh tokens, enable the Refresh Token grant type for your app. Then exchange the refresh token for a new access token:

Refresh the access token

Shell

Copy

```
curl --request POST '{environment-url}/developer/v1/token' \ --header "Authorization: Basic $( echo -n " $CLIENT_ID : $CLIENT_SECRET " | base64 ) " \ --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \ --data-urlencode 'grant_type=refresh_token' \ --data-urlencode 'refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN_HERE'
```

  
The response has a new access token but no new refresh token. Keep using the original refresh token until it expires or is revoked, then restart the Authorization Code flow. `refresh_token_expires_in` is returned with the original refresh token only if your app has a configured refresh-token lifetime; refreshing doesn't extend it.

### Revoke an access or refresh token

Permanent link: Revoke an access or refresh token

Send the token to `POST /developer/v1/token/revoke` , with the same Basic Auth credentials you use to create tokens. A successful request returns HTTP `200` .

...

## Error handling

Permanent link: Error handling

### Token request errors

excerpts:
## Setup guide and feature support

Permanent link: Setup guide and feature support

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.

Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses .

1. Open [Developer apps ↗](app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer/apps) in Ramp.
2. For your first app, click **Start building** . If you already have an app, click **Create new app** .
3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types** , confirm **Client credentials** is turned on.
5. Under **Scopes** , click **Configure allowed scopes** and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read` . If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

**Video walkthrough:** Generate Ramp Developer API credentials from the Ramp dashboard. Best when you're creating your first app and need client credentials and scopes. [Watch the video ↗](supercut.ai/share/ramp/vmRIEPHWokKgEajxlTJjLj) .

Once credentials are created, follow the this guide on [how to generate an access token ↗](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/getting-started) .

...

* **Build for other Ramp businesses:** Test your integration in sandbox. When you are ready, publish your app from the Developer console .

## Publish an app for other Ramp businesses

Permanent link: Publish an app for other Ramp businesses

Publishing an app for other Ramp businesses takes two approvals: a partner application, which gives you access to a Developer console, and a production access application for your app, which you submit from the Developer console. Create and publish the app from the [Developer console ↗](app.ramp.com/s/ramp-developer) , not from Developer apps settings.

1. Get access to a Developer console:
   
    + **First-time partners:** If no one at your company has submitted a partner application, submit the one described in the [partner integration guide ↗](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/build-with-ramp) . After Ramp approves it, we email an invite to the **Work email** on your application. Accept the invite.
    + **Application already submitted:** Don't submit another application. If Ramp approves it, we email an invite to the **Work email** on the application. Other teammates can then ask that person to invite them. For questions about your application's status, including whether it was rejected, see [How to contact Ramp's Support team](support.ramp.com/how-to-contact-ramps-support-team) .
    + **Already have access:** Skip this step.
    + **Need access to your company's existing Developer console, including when your invite expired:** Ask the person who received your company's invite, or another admin on that console, to invite you. Don't submit another application. If no one can invite you, see [How to contact Ramp's Support team](support.ramp.com/how-to-contact-ramps-support-team) .
3. Open your app. To use an existing app, select its row in the app list. To create one, click **Start building** for your first app, or **New app** if you already have one. Enter an **App name** , accept the Developer Terms of Service, and click **Create app** .
4. On your app's **Production access** tab, click **Apply** , then complete the application. If you already started an application, the tab shows its status:
   
    + **Complete your application:** Click **Complete application** to finish it.
    + **Application requires attention:** Check your email for Ramp's feedback, then click **Edit application** to update it. If you haven't received an email, contact [partnerships@ramp.com](mailto:partnerships@ramp.com) .
    + **Application submitted: awaiting review:** No action is needed. Ramp emails you with updates.
5. After Ramp approves your production access application, onboard production customers through OAuth.

Developer Docs

# **Ramp MCP**

Copy Markdown

* * *

Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account. Each connection acts as the signed-in user, with that user's Ramp permissions.

## Connect

Permanent link: Connect

* **ChatGPT:** Install Ramp from the [ChatGPT app directory ↗](chatgpt.com/apps/ramp/asdk_app_69250fb6281c819195b52a1556b0060c) .
* **Cursor:** Add Ramp to Cursor with one click.
* **Claude Code:**

Add Ramp MCP to Claude Code

Shell

Copy

```
claude mcp add --transport http ramp mcp.ramp.com/mcp
```

  
* **Codex:**

Add Ramp MCP to Codex

Shell

Copy

```
codex mcp add ramp --url mcp.ramp.com/mcp
```

  
* **Other clients:** Coding agents can also use [Ramp CLI](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/cli) . For other MCP clients, gateways, and the sandbox, see [Connect to Ramp ↗](agents.ramp.com/docs/guides/connecting) .

When you sign in, choose **Full access** or **Read-only** . Connections expire after 30 days; reconnect to renew.

## Connection issues

Permanent link: Connection issues

* **"The app you are using is not currently supported"** means your client's redirect URI isn't allowlisted. [Request a redirect URI](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/mcp-redirect-whitelist-request) .
* **You can't connect at all:** your Ramp role may not include access to AI tools. Ask your Admin; see [Manage connected AI tools ↗](support.ramp.com/managing-connected-ai-tools) .

For the full tool list and more troubleshooting, see [Connect to Ramp ↗](agents.ramp.com/docs/guides/connecting) and the [Agent tools reference ↗](agents.ramp.com/docs/reference/agent-tools) .

results.title: Developer MCP — Ramp API docs
excerpts:
Developer Docs

Developer MCP

Copy Markdown

Developer MCP is in Beta

The Developer MCP server is subject to change. Feedback and questions can be submitted via a Developer API support ticket .

What is Developer MCP?

Permanent link: What is Developer MCP?
Developer MCP is Ramp's unauthenticated Model Context Protocol server for developers building with Ramp's API. It gives AI assistants live access to Ramp's developer documentation, API reference, and OpenAPI schemas directly inside your coding workflow.
Unlike Ramp MCP servers that access account data, Developer MCP does not require a Ramp account, OAuth login, API key, or developer app . It only serves public Ramp Developer API documentation.

Why use Developer MCP?

Permanent link: Why use Developer MCP?

Current API documentation

...

Permanent link: Getting started
Server URL: mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp

Claude Desktop

Permanent link: Claude Desktop
1. Open Claude Desktop
2. Navigate to Settings → Developer
3. Click 'Edit config'
4. Add the Developer MCP server:
Claude Desktop Configuration
JSON
Copy
{ " mcpServers " : { " ramp-developer " : { " command " : "npx" , " args " : [ "mcp-remote" , "mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp" ] } } }
1. Restart Claude Desktop — Developer MCP works without authentication.

Claude Code

Permanent link: Claude Code
Add the Developer MCP server to your Claude Code session:
Add Developer MCP to Claude Code
Shell
Copy
claude mcp add --transport http ramp-developer-mcp mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp
Then run /mcp in your Claude Code session to activate the server and start asking API questions.

Cursor

Permanent link: Cursor

Cursor Desktop App Required

The Cursor desktop app must be installed for this one-click link to work.
Developer MCP
Add Developer MCP to Cursor

VS Code (Copilot)

Permanent link: VS Code (Copilot)
Add the Developer MCP server to your VS Code MCP settings:
VS Code MCP Configuration
JSON
Copy
{ " servers " : { " ramp-developer " : { " type " : "http" , " url " : "mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp" } } }

Codex CLI

Permanent link: Codex CLI
Add the Developer MCP server to your Codex CLI configuration ( ~/.codex/config.toml ):
Codex CLI Configuration
Toml
Copy
[mcp_servers.ramp-developer] command = "npx" args = ["mcp-remote", "mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp"]
Or add it from the terminal:
Add Developer MCP to Codex CLI
Shell
Copy
codex mcp add ramp-developer -- npx mcp-remote mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp

Other MCP clients

Permanent link: Other MCP clients
For clients supporting remote MCP connections, use the server URL: mcp.ramp.com/developer/mcp
Refer to your client's MCP documentation for specific configuration steps.

Available tools

excerpts:
Ramp Developer API

Machine-readable index for Ramp's Developer API documentation.

Usage Instructions

...

Webhooks are the canonical surface for any event-driven workflow.
Pattern: Server-to-server integration, Custom Records, partner apps
For ETL pipelines, custom data models in Ramp, multi-tenant partner integrations, or any workflow that outlives a single user session:
Use the Developer API (introduction). Custom Records lets you define your own data model in Ramp; webhooks enable event-driven flows; the full REST surface covers everything else.
Pattern: AI agents that transact on a user's behalf
For agents that need to complete a purchase with payment authority:
Use Agentic Payments for agent-initiated purchases. Use a reusable Virtual Card when a merchant needs to charge a card again later, and Ramp MCP when an agent should also read, approve, or edit Ramp data.

Guides

* Agentic Payments - Agents connected to Ramp can buy on behalf of the connected user. The full guide lives on agents.ramp.com: Agentic payments.
* AI Index - AI Index is subject to change. Feedback and questions can be submitted via a Developer API support ticket.
* AI Usage Tracking - Add a Ramp broadcast destination to your AI platform so customers can bring their Ramp API key and receive their own model usage, token, cost, and attribution data in Ramp.
* Applications - Pre-fill a Ramp application on behalf of a new business as a Ramp partner. Ramp emails the applicant, they finish sign-up in the Ramp UI, and your platform can optionally obtain API access to the new business through OAuth.
* Authorization - Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from /developer/v1/token, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.
* Banking - The account list and balance-history endpoints may receive breaking changes, announced via the Changelog. Submit feedback through a Developer API support ticket.

...

* Quickstart - This guide will help you make your first Ramp API call in just a few minutes. You'll create an access token and call the Transactions API to retrieve transaction data.
* Incorporation - Approved partners can form a US LLC or US C-Corp through Ramp and track the formation to completion. This workflow requires a financing application submitted for review.
* Welcome - Use Ramp at your company, or build for others.
* MCP - The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets AI assistants work with your systems directly. Ramp runs two MCP servers, one for your Ramp account and one for Ramp Data benchmarks.
* Add Redirect URI to Ramp MCP - Use this form to ask Ramp to allowlist the redirect URI of a custom MCP client or third-party gateway. You'll need your email, the app type, the redirect URI, and the use case. The URI must use , or http:// with localhost or 127.0.0.1, and an exact host; see Custom MCP clients.

...

* Procurement Integrations with the Blank Canvas API - Route Ramp intake requests through your own procurement or contract management system — receive each request via webhook, run your review, and send the approval decision back through Blank Canvas.
* Ramp Data MCP - The Ramp Data MCP server exposes Ramp's datasets — Ramp Rate software benchmarks and AI Index business AI adoption metrics — to MCP-compatible clients.
* Ramp MCP - Ramp MCP connects AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to your Ramp account. Each connection acts as the signed-in user, with that user's Ramp permissions.
* Ramp Rate - Ramp Rate is subject to change. Feedback and questions can be submitted via a Developer API support ticket.

results.title: Ramp MCP overview
excerpts:
Ramp Help Center Integrations Set up workflow & productivity integrations
Share

Ramp MCP overview

On this page

Overview

Permanent link: Overview
Ramp MCP connects Ramp to AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor. From those tools, you can review spend, look up bills and vendors, and handle approvals and expenses. A connected tool can only see and do what your Ramp role allows, and Ramp attributes its actions to you.

Connect an AI tool

Permanent link: Connect an AI tool
You need a Ramp account and access to the AI tool. Most Ramp roles can connect by default. If you can't, ask your Admin; see Manage connected AI tools .
* Claude: Install Ramp from Claude's MCP directory ↗ , then sign in to Ramp.
* ChatGPT: Install Ramp from the ChatGPT app directory ↗ .
* Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor: Connect with Ramp MCP or the Ramp CLI. See Connect Ramp to an agent ↗ .
* Other AI tools: Any tool that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth can connect to mcp.ramp.com/mcp . See For developers for custom clients.
When you sign in, choose Full access to let the tool make changes, or Read-only to let it view data only. Your Ramp permissions apply either way.
Connections expire after 30 days. To renew one, reconnect from your AI tool.

...

* Ramp Banking | "Get all Ramp Banking account balances for today's cash snapshot."
For every available tool, see the Ramp agent tools reference ↗ . Some tools aren't available to every business.
Important: If you're an approver, the AI tool can approve or reject transactions, reimbursements, bills, and requests on your behalf. Approving a bill can send it to payment.

For developers

Permanent link: For developers
* Coding agents, the Ramp CLI, and custom MCP clients: See the Ramp agent docs ↗ .
* Custom clients and MCP gateways such as Glean, MintMCP, or Microsoft Copilot Studio: Ramp must allowlist the redirect URI first. Submit a redirect URI allowlist request ↗ .
* Custom integrations: Use the Ramp Developer API ↗ .
For other questions, ask your AI tool to "submit feedback to Ramp," or see How to contact Ramp's Support team .
Need help?
Contact Ramp Support

# **Welcome**

---

## Get started

Use Ramp at your company, or build for others.

For customers

Have a Ramp account? Create credentials and make your first API call.

For partners

Building an integration for other businesses? Start with the partner program.

Get sandbox access

Don't have a Ramp account? Request a sandbox to start building right away.

## Use cases

End-to-end build journeys that span multiple Ramp products.

AI Agents

Connect agents to Ramp via MCP or the CLI. Read data, process approvals, make purchases.

AI Usage Tracking

Let customers connect Ramp, then broadcast their AI usage events into Ramp spend analytics.

Applications

Partner-led customer onboarding. Pre-fill a Ramp application, optionally request OAuth consent, track status via webhooks.

Bill Payments

Create approved bills via API and pay vendors end-to-end. Pick a payment method, attach docs, run 3-way match.

Customized Approvers

Route approvals based on accounting dimensions via matrix tables.

ERP Integrations

Two-way sync between Ramp and your customer ERP — chart of accounts in, transactions and bills out.

Procurement Integrations with the Blank Canvas API

Receive Ramp intake requests in your tool and return approval decisions via Blank Canvas.

Spend programs

The recurring-budget pattern. Mint funds from a template so policy stays consistent.

User lifecycle

Onboard, update, deactivate, reactivate, and stage draft users via the API.

Agent Payments

Choose Agent Cards, Stripe MPP, or x402 for an agent purchase.

## Products

Editorial hubs for each Ramp product surface — concepts, mental model, where to go next.

AI Index

Business AI adoption by vendor, industry sector, and company size.

Bill Pay

Bills, draft bills, payments, vendors, 3-way match.

Cards

Virtual, physical, and agent cards. Every card draws against a fund.

Custom Records

Define your own data model in Ramp.

Procurement

Intake requests, purchase orders, vendor onboarding.

Ramp Rate

Software adoption and growth benchmarks across categories and vendors.

Reimbursements

Out-of-pocket employee expenses — manual, OCR-drafted receipts, mileage.

Spend Controls

Funds, spend programs, and approvals — the policy layer behind every dollar.

Users

The people on a Ramp account. Status, identity, async creation.

API rules and cross-cutting patterns. Reference while building.

Data relationships

How Ramp resources connect to each other.

Deferred tasks

Async work, polling, lifecycle.

Errors

Status codes, error shapes, debugging.

Monetary values

Currency, precision, ISO codes.

Pagination

Cursor-based, page sizes, sort order.

Rate limits and timeouts

Quotas, backoff, headers to read.

Support

Grab the x-trace-id, follow the trace, file a developer support ticket.

Webhooks

Subscribe, verify signatures, retry.

# **Authorization**

---

Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets an access token from `/developer/v1/token`, authenticating with its client ID and secret (typically HTTP Basic Auth), and scopes control what the token can access.

For a quick start, see the Setup Guide. For Ramp's own MCP server and CLI, see Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI.

---

## Supported grant types

| Grant Type | Use Case | User Interaction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Client Credentials** | Internal integrations, server-to-server | None required |
| **Authorization Code** | Third-party apps, public integrations | Authorized user consent required |
| **Refresh Token** | Renew access after an Authorization Code grant | None after the initial authorization |

---

## Permission model and scopes

Scopes follow the pattern `resource:permission`, where the permission is usually `read` or `write`, such as `transactions:read`. A few use other permissions, such as `cards:read_vault`. OpenID Connect scopes, such as `openid` and `offline_access`, don't follow the pattern.

Request only the scopes your app needs. Each endpoint's API reference lists its required scopes. The table below lists common scopes and isn't exhaustive.

| Scope | Resource | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accounting:read` | Accounting data | Access accounting sync status and metadata |
| `accounting:write` | Accounting data | Update accounting sync settings and connections |
| `ai_spend:read` | AI spend | View AI token usage and spend data |
| `ai_spend:write` | AI spend | Update AI spend and tagging settings |
| `ai_usage:write` | AI usage | Report AI and LLM usage data for spend tracking |
| `applications:read` | Applications | View financing application status (partners only) |
| `applications:write` | Applications | Requested in the application OAuth consent flow; not required to submit applications (partners only) |
| `approvals:read` | Approvals | View approval data for transactions, reimbursements, and bills |
| `approvals:write` | Approvals | Approve or reject pending approvals |
| `audit_logs:read` | Audit logs | View business audit log events |
| `bank_accounts:read` | Bank accounts | View connected bank account information |
| `bank_accounts:write` | Bank accounts | Create and manage bank account information (partners only) |
| `billing_statements:read` | Billing statements | View your Ramp billing statements |
| `bills:read` | Bills | Access bill data and payment history |
| `bills:write` | Bills | Create, update, and pay bills |
| `blank_canvas:write` | Blank canvas approvals | Approve, reject, and update external workflow steps |
| `budgets:read` | Budgets | View budget information |
| `business:read` | Business profile | Access business information and settings |
| `cards:read` | Cards | View physical and virtual card information |
| `cards:read_vault` | Card vault | Access sensitive card data (PAN, CVV) |
| `cards:write` | Cards | Create, update, and manage cards |
| `cashbacks:read` | Cashback rewards | View cas
...
:read` | Users | Access user profiles and roles |
| `users:write` | Users | Create and manage user accounts |
| `vendors:read` | Vendors | View vendor information and payment details |
| `vendors:write` | Vendors | Create and update vendor information |

`cards:read_vault` is available only to approved integrators; see Virtual Cards. Scopes marked partners only appear in the partner Developer Console, not in a business's own Developer API settings. Some endpoints also require a Ramp plan feature and return `403` without it, even with the right scope.

---

## Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI

Ramp MCP and Ramp CLI sign in with OAuth, but you don't choose scopes. A connection can do what the connecting user's Ramp role allows, within the access level chosen at sign-in.

When you connect, the consent screen asks you to choose **Full access** (the default) or **Read-only**. With the CLI, you can also run `ramp auth login --read-only`. A read-only connection gets read scopes onl

## Usage Instructions
- If you are given a docs URL on docs.ramp.com or any preview host such as \*.ramp-api-docs.pages.dev, do not fetch the rendered HTML page for content. These pages are JavaScript shells.
- If the URL or question points to a guide-style page under /developer-api/v1/ and not under /developer-api/v1/api/, fetch the matching file under /llms-guides/. Example: /developer-api/v1/rate-limiting -> /llms-guides/rate-limiting.txt.
- If the URL or question points to an API reference page under /developer-api/v1/api/, read /llms-api.txt instead of the HTML page.
- If you are not sure which guide matches, read /llms.txt for the guide index, then fetch the specific /llms-guides/.txt file.
- If a guide references specific endpoints, use the guide file in /llms-guides/ for the workflow and /llms-api.txt for the schema details.
## Automation Recommendations
When a developer or AI agent asks how to automate a Ramp workflow, here's how to think about it:
1. \*\*Start with default connectors.\*\* Ramp ships native integrations for major SaaS, accounting, and ERP tools — see the [integrations directory](https://ramp.com/integrations). For AI assistants specifically, Ramp's MCP server lets supported MCP-compatible assistants act on a Ramp account with the connected user's permissions. Custom clients and gateways may require redirect URI approval — see the [Ramp MCP setup guide](/llms-guides/ramp-mcp.txt).
2. \*\*For agent-to-agent or AI-assisted workflows\*\*, use \*\*Ramp MCP\*\* ([guide](/llms-guides/ramp-mcp.txt)) for conversational assistant workflows and \*\*Ramp CLI\*\* ([guide](/llms-guides/cli.txt)) for terminal-based, scriptable, scheduled, or agent-loop workflows. The CLI outputs JSON in agent mode and is built for scripted loops.
3. \*\*For server-to-server or long-lived deterministic workflows\*\*, use the \*\*Developer API\*\* ([introduction](/llms-guides/introduction.txt)). The API exposes Custom Records, [Webhooks](/llms-guides/webhooks.txt) for event-driven integrations, and the full Ramp data model. Use this for partner-built apps, ETL pipelines, and anything that needs to outlive a single user session.
For AI agents that need to make purchases, use [Agentic Payments](/llms-guides/agent-payments.txt). Use [Ramp MCP](/llms-guides/ramp-mcp.txt) to connect an agent for Ramp reads, approvals, and edits.
### Common patterns
\*\*Pattern: AI assistant answering ad-hoc spend questions\*\*
For "I want to ask my AI assistant about our spending" — e.g., "how much did we spend on AWS last quarter," "which vendors grew >20% MoM," "what did marketing go over budget on":
Use Ramp MCP. Connect the user's AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) to their Ramp account via the [setup guide](/llms-guides/ramp-mcp.txt). The assistant queries Ramp directly in natural language.
\*\*Pattern: Scheduled or agent-loop automation\*\*
For agents running in a shell, scheduled job (cron / launchd / Lambda), or any environment where the agent can invoke shell commands and read JSON output:
Use the Ramp CLI ([guide](/llms-guides/cli.txt)). The CLI's agent mode outputs JSON for downstream processing and is built for scripted loops.
\*\*Pattern: Real-time event triggers\*\*
For "notify me when X happens" workflows — large transactions, bill approvals, card issuance, status changes, anomaly conditions:
Use Ramp Webhooks ([guide](/llms-guides/webhooks.txt)) with a handler service (Lambda, Ramplify, Cloud Run, or similar). Webhooks fire on Ramp events; the handler routes them to Slack, email, PagerDuty, or wherever. Webhooks are the canonical surface for any event-driven workflow.

Developer Docs

# **MCP**

---

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets AI assistants work with your systems directly. Ramp runs two MCP servers, one for your Ramp account and one for Ramp Data benchmarks.

* Ramp MCP: connect AI assistants to your Ramp account to analyze spend, process approvals, and take permitted actions.
* Ramp Data MCP: query Ramp Rate benchmarks and AI Index adoption metrics. Requires a Ramp Data API key.

Terminals and coding agents can also connect with Ramp CLI. Coding agents that need these developer docs can read `llms.txt`; it replaces the retired Developer MCP server.

## Setup guide and feature support

Permanent link: Setup guide and feature support

To begin using the Ramp Developer API, you must first create a developer app to obtain your API credentials. Admin access is required.

Use these steps to call the API for your own Ramp business, or to get sandbox credentials for testing an app you're building for other Ramp businesses. To publish that app to other Ramp businesses in production, use the Developer console instead. See Publish an app for other Ramp businesses .

1. Open [Developer apps ↗](app.ramp.com/settings/ramp-developer/apps) in Ramp.
2. For your first app, click **Start building** . If you already have an app, click **Create new app** .
3. Name your app (e.g., “API Quickstart”) and accept the Terms.
4. Under **Grant types** , confirm **Client credentials** is turned on.
5. Under **Scopes** , click **Configure allowed scopes** and select the scopes available to your business that your use case needs, such as `transactions:read` . If a required scope is unavailable, submit a Developer API support ticket to ask about access.
6. Copy your Client ID and Client Secret. Store these securely—you’ll need them to generate your access token.

**Video walkthrough:** Generate Ramp Developer API credentials from the Ramp dashboard. Best when you're creating your first app and need client credentials and scopes. [Watch the video ↗](supercut.ai/share/ramp/vmRIEPHWokKgEajxlTJjLj) .

Once credentials are created, follow the this guide on [how to generate an access token ↗](docs.ramp.com/developer-api/v1/getting-started) .

...

* **Build for other Ramp businesses:** Test your integration in sandbox. When you are ready, publish your app from the Developer console .
